'''Fa-Yueh Wu''' (January 5, 1932 – January 21, 2020) was a Chinese-born theoretical physicist, mathematical physicist, and mathematician who studied and contributed to solid-state physics and statistical mechanics.

== Life ==
=== Early stage ===
{{no refs|section|date=September 2023}}
Born on January 5, 1932, in [[Shimen County]], [[Hunan Province]], [[Republic of China (1912–1949)|Republic of China]], with his father, a member of the Legislature, as his fourth child. The [[temporary capital]] of the [[Chiang Kai-shek]] administration of [[Nationalist government]] was placed in [[Chongqing]] in December 1938, but before that, in 1937, he evacuated to Chongqing with his father and stepmother<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.currentobituary.com/obit/240200|title=Professor Fa Yueh|website=www.currentobituary.com}}</ref> and entered an elementary school there. However, due to repeated [[Bombing of Chongqing]], he was unable to settle in one place. In 1943, he enrolled in [[Nankai University|Nankai Junior High School]], which was evacuated to Chongqing at the time. He transferred to a high school in [[Nanjing]], which became the capital of Chiang Kai-shek administration again in 1946, after the collapse of [[Wang Jingwei regime]]. In 1948 he moved to [[Changsha]] and transferred to another junior high school. In 1949, he fled to [[Taiwan]] with his father and stepmother due to the [[Chinese Civil War]], but separated from the four siblings who remained on the continent. His parents died without being able to resume with their children.

=== Republic of China Navy ===
He enrolled in the [[Republic of China Navy]] Mechanical School in 1949, entered the Department of Electrical Engineering a year later, earned a bachelor's degree in 1954, served in the Republic of China Navy from 1954 to 1956, and became a lieutenant in the Navy. In 1955, he was selected to study radar engineering for half a year in San Francisco, USA. He was an expert of [[radar]] and [[sonar]]. He was also a master of [[Xiangqi]].

=== Physics ===
He entered the [[National Tsing Hua University]] in 1957 and received a master's degree from the Institute of Atomic Sciences Physics Group in June 1959. He then went to the United States on a scholarship to study many-body problems <ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S021797920201155X?journalCode=ijmpb|title=FA YUEH WU &#124; International Journal of Modern Physics B|doi=10.1142/S021797920201155X |url-access=subscription}}</ref> under [[Eugene Feenberg]]<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.122.739|title=Ground State of Liquid Helium (Mass 4)|first1=Fa Yueh|last1=Wu|first2=Eugene|last2=Feenberg|date=May 1, 1961|journal=Physical Review|volume=122|issue=3|pages=739–742|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.122.739|bibcode=1961PhRv..122..739W |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.128.943|title=Theory of the Fermion Liquid|first1=Fa Yueh|last1=Wu|first2=Eugene|last2=Feenberg|date=October 15, 1962|journal=Physical Review|volume=128|issue=2|pages=943–955|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.128.943|bibcode=1962PhRv..128..943W |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>[https://academic.oup.com/ptp/article/28/3/568/1846169 The Ground State of Liquid He<sup>4</sup> 1962]</ref> at [[Washington University in St. Louis]], and received his PhD in 1963.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.phys.sinica.edu.tw/~tywufund//download/camp/2004/cv/cv_camp2004_FaYuehWu.pdf|title=Fa-Yueh Wu}}</ref>  He was an assistant professor at [[Virginia Tech]] in 1963 and [[Northeastern University]] in 1967, an associate professor in 1969, and a professor in 1975. He has been a university professor since 1989 and Matthews professor since 1992. He has numerous academic treatises.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://id.oclc.org/worldcat/entity/E39PBJq6XjvKPvfCcKWVXHXTpP.html|title=Fa-Yueh Wu|website=id.oclc.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://coek.info/pdf-fa-yueh-wu-curriculum-vitae-.html%E3%80%80FA-YUEH|url-status=|title=Curriculum vitae|website=coek.info}}{{deadlink|date=September 2023}}</ref> In 1976, Wu was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=Fa%20Yueh%20Wu&af=true |access-date=31 March 2026 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> After he retired in 2006, he became an emeritus professor. He died at his home in Newton, Massachusetts, on January 21, 2020.

== Books ==
